videos.script: DeepEval and RAGAS do what the last four lessons did by hand, inside a structure: a test case, a metric, a runner. {{structure}} Before the first run, three things. Both send telemetry unless told not to. DeepEval keeps every test case on disk. And RAGAS needed three packages pinned before it would import. {{install}} Most of their metrics are prompts to a model, several per reply. With the local model as judge, DeepEval's faithfulness gets the contradiction right, and explains it wrongly. {{asks}} Run on all forty-eight replies, it scores fewer than half. Of eleven it fails, one is unfaithful. The course's own checks, inside the same runner, give the same counts as before. {{own}} RAGAS's string metrics agree with ours. Its model-graded relevancy scores fourteen replies of forty-eight, and none of the refusals. {{recall}} Read a metric before you run it, count what it could not score, and measure it before you trust it. {{end}}
